data.cultural_impact: The name "Ruyah" in Islamic culture is often associated with the concept of life force, signifying the breath of life or the spirit that animates the body. This could be derived from the Arabic root "ruyya", which means breath or wind. In some Islamic traditions, it is believed that Allah (God) breathes the soul into a person at the moment of their birth and takes it back at the moment of their death. Thus, the name "Ruyah" could be considered a reminder of the divine presence within each individual, as well as the fragility and transient nature of life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Ruyah" is a reminder of the invisible yet powerful force that sustains us and connects us to the divine. It is a reminder of the breath of Allah (God), which gives us life and nourishment, and ultimately returns us to the source from which we came. The name "Ruyah" invites us to reflect on the preciousness of life and to appreciate the sacred gift of consciousness. It also encourages us to cultivate a deep sense of gratitude and reverence for the mysteries of existence. In this way, the name "Ruyah" serves as a source of inspiration and motivation for us to live our lives with intention, purpose and meaning.
